source: In private trials, however, no choice feedback was displayed, a yellow border surrounded the offer and a picture of a padlock was displayed on the top of the screen (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the visual cues for private trials.

claim: Subjects were told to respond within 1 s, otherwise a message reminded them to respond.
source: Subjects were told to respond within 1 s, otherwise a message reminded them to respond.
evidence: This describes the response time instructions.

claim: Instructions emphasized that accuracy was more important than speed during choices.
source: Instructions emphasized that accuracy was more important than speed during choices.
evidence: This describes the task instructions.

claim: Mixed-effect regression analysis was used to fit two models to the data separately for each organization.
source: Separately for each organization, two models were fit to the data using mixed-effect regression analysis in STATA v.10.
evidence: This describes the statistical analysis approach.

claim: Separate models were set up for choices concerning the good organization versus the bad organization because these choices were paired with diametrically opposite material consequences.
source: We set up separate models for choices concerning the good organization versus the bad organization, since these choices were paired in our design with diametrically opposite material consequences (material costs versus material gains, respectively).
evidence: This describes the rationale for separate models.

claim: A Magstim super-rapid stimulator was used to stimulate both cortical sites using a 7 cm figure of eight-coil.
source: A Magstim super-rapid stimulator (Magstim, Whitland, Dyfed, UK) was used to stimulate both cortical sites using a 7 cm figure of eight-coil.
evidence: This describes the TMS equipment used.

claim: The active motor threshold (AMT) was defined as the minimal stimulus intensity required to produce MEPs of ≥200 mV amplitude in ≥5 of 10 consecutive pulses.
source: The AMT was defined as the minimal stimulus intensity required to produce MEPs of ≥200 mV amplitude in ≥5 of 10 consecutive pulses.
evidence: This describes the definition of active motor threshold.

claim: A distance-correction for differences in scalp-cortex distance method was applied after obtaining the stimulation output from the hotspot.
source: After obtaining the stimulation output from the hotspot, a distance-correction for differences in scalp-cortex distance method was applied (Stokes et al., 2007).
evidence: This describes a correction method applied, with a citation.

claim: The protocol resulted in an average stimulation output of 39%.
source: This protocol resulted in an average stimulation output of 39% (range 31–56), using intensity of 80% of each individual's AMT for the hand.
evidence: This provides the average stimulation intensity.

claim: Target sites were localized using the Brainsight frameless stereotaxy system with a Polaris infrared tracking system.
source: Target sites were localized using the Brainsight frameless stereotaxy system (Rogue Research, Montreal Canada) with a Polaris (NorthernDigital, Waterloo, Canada) infrared tracking system.
evidence: This describes the neuronavigation system used.

claim: Theta burst stimulation (TBS) applying repeated burst of 3 pulses at 50 Hz is known to deactivate the stimulated neurons during 30 min when applied continuously.
source: We used theta burst stimulation (TBS) applying repeated burst of 3 pulses at 50 Hz, known to deactivate the stimulated neurons during 30 min (Huang et al., 2005) when applied continuously.
evidence: This describes the TBS protocol and its effects, with a citation.

claim: Every TBS burst was repeated at a 5 Hz rate resulting in 200 bursts with a total of 600 pulses.
source: Every TBS burst was repeated at a 5 Hz rate resulting in 200 bursts with a total of 600 pulses.
evidence: This describes the TBS parameters.

claim: For TPJ TBS, the coil was placed with the handle perpendicular to the supramarginal gyrus anterior to TPJ.
source: For TPJ TBS, the coil was placed with the handle perpendicular to the supramarginal gyrus anterior to TPJ (with the current going in the anterior to posterior direction)
evidence: This describes the coil placement for TPJ stimulation.

claim: For the vertex TBS, the coil was held parallel to the midline.
source: and for the vertex TBS it was held parallel to the midline.
evidence: This describes the coil placement for vertex stimulation.

claim: TBS was applied using online tracking system held by a robotic arm to guarantee correct placement during TBS period.
source: TBS was applied using online tracking system held by a robotic arm to guarantee correct placement during TBS period.
evidence: This describes the method for maintaining coil position during stimulation.

claim: Several questionnaires were employed to measure the participants' personality characteristics, Machiavellism levels, social orientation, impulsiveness and their willingness to help others.
source: To check that the decisions were not influenced by individual differences in personality and predispositions for types of social behavior, we employed several questionnaires to measure the participants' personality characteristics (International Personality Item Pool, IPIP), Machiavellism levels (Mach IV Scale), social orientation (Social Value Orientation, SVO), impulsiveness (Barratt impulsive scale- III) and their willingness to help others (Prosocial Personality Battery, PSB).
evidence: This describes the personality assessments conducted.

claim: Personality characteristics that could interfere with social interactions were assessed using the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale (SIAS).
source: Personality characteristics that could interfere with social interactions (such as fear of being observed) were also assessed (Social Interaction Anxiety Scale, SIAS).
evidence: This describes an additional personality assessment.

claim: A questionnaire was designed to obtain precise information of subject's beliefs about the experimental set-up.
source: Finally, we designed a questionnaire to obtain precise information of subject's beliefs about the experimental set-up (i.e. how observed they felt, how they perceived the cTBS, etc).
evidence: This describes a custom questionnaire used in the study.

claim: Groups had similar personality measures that did not differ significantly due to the randomization process.
source: Supplementary file 1 shows that groups had similar personality measures that did not differ significantly due to our randomization process.
evidence: This is a finding from the personality assessments.

claim: Measures of each subject valuation of each organization were obtained to ensure no between-group differences coexisted in the behavioral results.
source: We obtained measures of each subject valuation of each organization to ensure no between-group differences coexisted in the behavioral results.
evidence: This describes the rationale for the organization ratings.

claim: The good organization was rated higher overall than the bad organization.
source: As expected, the good organization was rated higher overall than the bad organization (see Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the organization ratings.

claim: The valuation of organizations was not different between the cTBS and sham groups.
source: Importantly, the valuation of organizations was not different between the cTBS and sham groups (F > 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the organization ratings.
